value.first: For a 2-year-old moving out of your bed, I'd use the chair method (camping out). It was one of the two arms in a randomized trial, and the five-year follow-up found no differences either way in behaviour, sleep or the parent-child relationship - it's slower than timed check-ins, but it's the one that works for a toddler who can climb out and follow you. Graduated check-ins need a crib and a closed door, so they're not the fit here.
value.second: Set up her own safe sleep space and pick a start night with no travel or illness ahead. Bedtime 6:30-8:00, same 20-30 minute wind-down every night: bath, book, bed, with any milk before the book. Put her down awake and sit in a chair right beside her - calm presence, minimal touch, no rocking or feeding to sleep. Nights 1-3 there, then move the chair mid-room, then by the door, then the hallway in view, then gone. About 3 nights per spot, 2-3 weeks total.
value.third: Treat every night waking the same way: walk her back, same chair position you're on, same short phrase. Expect less intense crying than timed methods but more nights of protest - consistency for the full 2-3 weeks is the whole mechanism. Never latch her door shut or hold her in bed. If she snores, mouth-breathes or has breathing pauses in sleep, get her checked - no behavioural method fixes that. I'll check in Friday.
